sub_questions.question: Why does it say I'm out of credits when I haven't used the app much?
Can you fix this (restore the ability to use the app)?

claims.claim: Credit allowance differs depending on the plan.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew)

claims.claim: On the free Sandbox plan, the 200 message credits are a one-time allowance that does not renew.
Even light use can exhaust the Sandbox credit allowance.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models ... around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: On Professional or Team, credits reset monthly.
claims.guide_evidence: waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans)

claims.claim: Running out mid-cycle usually means a heavier model, with some responses costing more credits than others, burned through the balance faster.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: The customer can check the plan and remaining credits on the Billing page.
claims.guide_evidence: Only the workspace owner and admins can open the Billing page and manage a subscription.

claims.claim: Connecting your own provider key is an option to resolve running out of credits.
claims.guide_evidence: model calls on Dify-hosted credits stop working until the workspace either connects its own API key for that provider

claims.claim: A one-time courtesy credit top-up is available and can usually be approved within a day.

customer_safety_issues: Promises a courtesy credit top-up approved within a day, which the guide does not mention; the customer may wait for it instead of connecting a key or upgrading.
evaluation.rationale: The answer correctly explains how credits work: Sandbox credits are one-time, paid-plan credits reset monthly, and heavier models use more credits. Asking which plan the customer is on is a sensible clarifying question. But it also offers a "one-time courtesy credit top-up, which we can usually approve within a day," which the guide never mentions. That is an unsupported commercial promise the customer could rely on, so the answer isn't safe to send as is.
